title: Cohort-driven latency auditor and prefill/decode scheduler simulator
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: Current CI perf gates and golden baselines catch some regressions, but they lack sensitivity to cohort-specific latency regressions that arise from kernel dispatch changes and attention-path optimizations. Small kernel routing tweaks or prefill/decode schedule shifts can create 20-200ms regressions for specific traffic cohorts (short-chat, long-prefill, multi-turn streaming).

Goal: Build an auditor + simulator that can: (1) partition our canonical workload corpus into operational cohorts (by seq-len distribution, token-conditional branching, streaming vs batch), (2) run a kernel-dispatch simulator to predict latency impact of kernel-routing heuristics and attention-threading options, and (3) surface cohort-level regression signals as CI perf gates with explainable contributing factors.

Deliverables:
- Cohort generator that tags canonical workloads into stable cohorts with metadata (p50/p95 seq len, avg kv cache reuse, streaming flag).
- Kernel dispatch simulator: lightweight deterministic model that consumes a kernel-routing policy and workload cohort and emits per-op latency estimates and tokenized latency timelines. Simulator will be validated against golden trace runs.
- Prefill/decode scheduler simulator that models KV-cache warmup, prefill chunking, and jitter from batching; outputs end-to-end latency distribution for prefill+first-decode and steady-state decode.
- CI perf gate integration: cohort-level delta metrics (p50/p95/p99, tail-splitting) and automatic attribution hints (most likely kernel or schedule change).
- Dashboard and smoke reports: cohort heatmap, timeline diff viewer, example failing traces and links to reproducible runs.

Non-goals: full fidelity micro-kernel timing (we will validate with golden runs, but the simulator is intentionally slightly coarser to be CI-light). We will not change kernel routing heuristics as part of this ticket; only measure and surface effects.

Success criteria:
- New CI gate triggers on a staged kernel-routing change that produced a known 120ms regression for the long-prefill cohort in internal experiments.
- False positive rate < 2% across 2 weeks of canary runs.
- Observability: engineers can drill from gate failure to the top 3 candidate causes (kernel choice, batch cadence, prefill chunk size) and a reproducible benchmark run link within 10 minutes.
acceptance_criteria: Cohort generator produces stable cohorts and can re-run nightly to incorporate new traces.
Simulator validated against at least 5 golden trace runs with mean error < 10% for p50/p95 latency estimates.
CI integration posts cohort deltas and blocks PRs when p95 increases by > 10% for a high-impact cohort.
Dashboard shows heatmap, time-diff, and direct links to reproducible runner artifacts (GCS/bench job).
